description: PowerDynamics.jl represents grid machines, controllers and lines as equation-based components and assembles a differential-algebraic system. ModelingToolkit, NetworkDynamics and Julia differential-equation tools support component initialisation and simulation. The provider is JuliaEnergy and PowerDynamics contributors. Coverage: The software is generic, not a measured geographic dataset. Spatial detail and simulation periods are supplied by the user. Access: The public source repository provides documentation and installation instructions. Source archives and dependencies were not downloaded or run. Licence and cost: The README describes open-source software. The precise repository licence requires reading its licence file before redistribution. Limitations: The README names continuing 2024–2027 development and a validation publication. Validation claims were not independently reproduced and do not establish every custom component’s accuracy. For simulation it supports dynamic power-grid modelling and disturbance-response analysis. Related resources: No existing catalogue record explicitly covers PowerDynamics.jl.
